subject: Clarify hosted API latency commitments and proposed grace/carveout approach
messages:
From: Jake Mullins <jake@finwell.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarification: Hosted API latency commitments and handling of transient spikes

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Finwell's infra team is reviewing Redwood for several customer-facing routing features. Before we move forward we'd like a clearer picture of the Hosted API latency commitments and how Redwood treats transient spikes. A few specific questions:

- Can you confirm the p50 and p95 token-response targets you publish for the Hosted API and whether those are global or region-specific?
- How are measurement windows defined? (rolling window, fixed buckets, alignment to wall clock?)
- Do you have a formal grace / shortfall policy for transient bursts or maintenance events (examples: 10-minute outage, sustained 5m tail latency spikes)?
- Is there a carveout when a customer has a burst traffic pattern (e.g., product launch) and what is the request process for a temporary exception?

We're trying to map this back to our SLIs so we can present an internal risk/acceptance plan. If useful, CCing our platform alias: platform@finwell.com.

Appreciate the details — if you can send a short bulleted response or a draft addendum we can review, that would be ideal.

Best,
Jake Mullins
Head of Platform, Finwell Health

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Clarification: Hosted API latency commitments and handling of transient spikes

Kim / Marissa — summary of how we measure and what options look like (technical note to include in the addendum). Putting the short version up front, then details/examples.

Short version (recommended defaults):
- Published targets (Hosted API, us-east region): p50 = ~80 ms server-side token time, p95 = ~220 ms. These are measured server-to-server (Redwood edge to model executor) for standard text-generation requests.
- Measurement model: rolling 1-hour windows for alerting and a rolling 24-hour window for monthly SLO calculation. Percentiles computed on per-request latencies (end-to-end server processing) with a 99th-outlier-trimming stage for noisy samples.
- Transient carveouts: automated transient shortfall carveout where up to 10 minutes of aggregate shortfall per incident can be excluded if caused by platform maintenance or regional networking events. Monthly allowance of 3% of total measurement time as a transient carveout pool (subject to review).
- Temporary exception (customer-driven burst): we offer a time-boxed exception for planned launches where we: 1) reserve additional burst capacity (dedicated pool or increased quota), 2) set a temporary monitoring window with relaxed p95 threshold, and 3) document the dates/times in an appendix. Requests must be submitted 72 hours in advance for capacity changes.

Details and examples:
- Measurement windows: we use overlapping rolling windows. Alerts are triggered on 1h rolling windows (if p95 exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive 10-minute samples) to catch short regressions. Monthly SLOs are aggregated from rolling 24h windows to smooth transient effects.
- Outlier trimming: samples with external network time > 50% of total latency or requests that are retried due to client cancellations are excluded from percentile computation.
- Grace policy example: if a regional maintenance causes 12 minutes of elevated p95 in a single incident, the first 10 minutes are automatically carved out; the remaining 2 minutes count against the SLO unless a post-incident review justifies an extended carveout.
- API examples: we can tag routes/endpoints so the SLO applies only to the "chat.sync" route while embeddings routes use a different quantile. Tagging is done via the Route config in the Console.

I've attached a small CSV with hypothetical incident examples and how they'd flow through the math (slo-examples.csv). Happy to expand with additional scenarios you care about.

Rishi
Inference SRE
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): slo-examples.csv (CSV, 28KB)

Hi Jake — thanks for the patience. Below is a concise, customer-facing summary you can include in your risk assessment. Where useful I added suggested wording for a short-term addendum.

Customer-facing summary (recommended wording):
- Published Hosted API targets (us regions): p50 = 80 ms; p95 = 220 ms. These are measured on a per-request basis server-side and reported in our Console per-route.
- Measurement windows: Rolling 1-hour windows for alerting; rolling 24-hour windows for monthly SLO computation. Percentiles are computed after removing clear network outliers and client cancellations.
- Grace/carveout policy: We provide an automatic 10-minute incident carveout for platform maintenance or regional network interruptions. Additionally, customers have a monthly transient allowance equal to 3% of measurement time that can be applied to short-term bursts.
- Planned-burst exceptions: For planned launches we offer a 72-hour request workflow to reserve burst capacity and a time-boxed SLO relaxation documented in an addendum.

Proposed next steps tailored to Finwell (what I recommend we sign as an addendum):
1) Scope: Apply the SLO addendum to "chat.sync" and "ingest.batch" endpoints only.
2) Carveout: Apply the standard 10-minute automatic carveout plus a 3% monthly transient allowance.
3) Planned burst: Finwell to submit a launch request 72 hours before the event; Redwood will provision burst capacity where available and record a time-limited exception.
4) Operational runbook: Marissa will run a 30-minute walkthrough with Finwell's on-call about thresholds and escalation steps.

If that sounds acceptable I'll: 1) send the SLA-addendum-draft with the Finwell-specific scope filled in, 2) kick off legal for a brief addendum, and 3) provide the DocuSign link for signature.

Let me know which endpoints you want in scope and any dates for planned launches.

Thanks,
Kim
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
